renderings.technical:
### Changed

- Integrate the complete M9 frontend redesign milestone into `main` as one coherent branch, combining the two divergent halves that were built off v1.8.0, and add the v1.9.0 release notes so the release can be tagged from a single point. ([#244](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/244))

### Added

- Re-introduce inline citation badges in the assistant's sanitized Markdown answer, anchored after each cited passage title, with a hover and focus tooltip showing source, heading and snippet, and with citations listed in the sources section numbered to match. ([#245](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/245))
- Make the most likely next step from `SuggestedNextSteps` a primary button in the ticket header that executes the routed action, with remaining steps in an overflow menu and unmappable steps shown as non-clickable text. ([#237](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/237))
- Add a `Ctrl/Cmd+K` command palette available on every page, offering navigation entries generated from `NavRegistry` and debounced, cancellable ticket search, operable fully by keyboard, and restoring focus on close. ([#236](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/236))
- Apply ticket status changes optimistically on the board and the ticket detail view, roll back to the previous state with a snackbar showing the error code when the server rejects a transition, and ignore superseded moves so the board never holds a status the server did not accept. ([#235](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/235))
- Replace the assign and change-status dialogs with inline popover menus anchored to the ticket header that apply changes in place through the existing command handlers, without navigating or opening a modal. ([#234](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/234))
- Anchor assistant citations to the answer text as inline badges with a hover and keyboard-focus tooltip, keep a numbered sources list for citations not anchored inline, and leave answers without citations unchanged. ([#233](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/233))
- Inject the active agent roster into the assistant's chat system prompt on every request, instructing the model to use exactly those names and list valid agents rather than guess when a name is not on the roster. ([#221](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/221))
- Force the `check_grounding` tool through `tool_choice` once after knowledge-base passages are retrieved in a run, for both the interactive assistant and the autonomous worker, so the grounding verdict is computed before the first streamed token. ([#218](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/218))
- Centralize palette, spacing, radius, elevation and semantic chip colors as design tokens rendered as CSS custom properties and shared with the MudBlazor theme, replacing hard-coded literals across scoped stylesheets, and change `KpiCard.Accent` to a tone enum. ([#213](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/213))

### Fixed

- Wrap the board card title in a row element so its two-line `-webkit-line-clamp` with ellipsis applies, and keep card titles from shrinking below their content width. ([#240](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/240))
- Target the assistant chat panel through a deep selector so its padding and flex column layout apply, keeping the composer send button inside the panel at all widths. ([#239](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/239))
- Give the Category column in the ticket queue a fixed width and render its header in uppercase like its neighbours, so it no longer overlaps the Due header, while keeping it a static label because it is not a sort field. ([#238](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/238))
- Add a system prompt paragraph telling the assistant never to state a change happened without a successful tool result in the conversation, and not to ask for confirmation of writes the user already requested unless a genuine decision is needed. ([#223](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/223))
- Render ticket summary timestamps in the configured user timezone, including created, due and comment times, and state the zone in the prompt header so the model reports local times. ([#222](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/222))
- Return an error result from the knowledge-base search tool when a non-transient failure occurs, distinct from the unavailable result, so the dashboard error rate reflects real failures, while transient faults still rethrow for retry. ([#220](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/220))
- Score grounding by meaning, comparing each substantive answer sentence against retrieved passages with embeddings and falling back to the lexical evaluator when embeddings are unavailable or fail. ([#219](https://github.com/goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite/pull/219))
renderings.customer:
### What's New

- **Inline citation badges:** Answers that cite a source can now show a numbered badge right after the cited passage title, with the source, heading and a snippet in a hover or focus tooltip. The sources list uses the same numbers, so you can match a badge to its entry directly.
- **Suggested next step as a button:** The most likely next step for a ticket now appears as a primary button that carries out the action when clicked. Other suggested steps sit behind an overflow menu, and steps that cannot be run from the header are shown as text only.
- **Command palette on Ctrl+K:** Pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) opens a command palette from any page. It lists the navigation destinations and matches tickets as you type, and you can move through the results and open one using only the keyboard.
- **Immediate status updates:** A status change on the ticket board or detail view now shows immediately. If the server rejects the change, the ticket returns to its previous status and a message gives the reason code.
- **Status and assignee changes in place:** Changing a ticket's status or assignee is done from a menu in the ticket header. The ticket stays open and keeps its scroll position and current tab, so you no longer get pulled into a separate dialog.
- **Citations in assistant answers:** Assistant answers now show citations as badges placed where the answer uses them, and hovering or focusing a badge shows the source, heading and snippet. Citations the answer does not reference are listed below it, and answers without citations look as before.
- **Agent names known to the assistant:** The assistant now knows the names of the active agents when it answers, so it can name valid agents directly. If a requested name is not on the roster, it lists the valid names rather than guessing a close match.
- **Grounding check always runs:** When the assistant has retrieved knowledge-base passages, it now checks its answer against them before responding, so the check no longer depends on the model choosing to run it.
- **Consistent visual styling:** The interface uses one set of colours, spacing and corner radii across all pages, and the status and priority tags look the same wherever they appear.

### What's Changed

- **Frontend Redesign release:** The release v1.9.0 brings the Frontend Redesign milestone into the main branch.

### Bug Fixes

- **Board card titles clipped:** Long ticket titles on the board are now cut off after two lines with an ellipsis, so cards in a column keep a consistent height.
- **Assistant send button placement:** The send button in the assistant's message box now stays inside the panel, and the text field and button stay aligned at narrow widths.
- **Ticket queue column header:** The Category column in the ticket queue no longer overlaps the Due column, and its header matches the other column headers in uppercase.
- **Assistant change confirmations:** The assistant no longer states that a change was made unless the change was actually carried out and reported as successful, and it makes a requested change without asking again.
- **Summary timestamps in your timezone:** Timestamps in the streamed ticket summary now match the times shown in the ticket detail view in your timezone.
- **Failed knowledge-base searches reported:** A failed knowledge-base search is now reported as an error, distinct from a search that found nothing, so the dashboard's error rate reflects real failures.
- **Grounding check by meaning:** The grounding check now compares the meaning of answer sentences with the retrieved passages, so a correct paraphrase or a translation is no longer marked as ungrounded.
